elements.quote: “A living systematic review of the literature was designed”
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly describes the work as a (living) systematic review.

elements.quote: “The objective of this study is to identify the best available scientific evidence on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the mental health of out-of-hospital HPs in terms of stress, anxiety, depression, and self-efficacy.”
elements.reason: The abstract provides an explicit statement of the main objective.

elements.quote: “Original research was selected, published in either English, Spanish, French, Italian, or Portuguese.”
elements.reason: The abstract states part of the inclusion criteria (original research and publication languages), but it does not specify the full main inclusion/exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: “consulting the electronic online versions of the CINHAL, Cochrane Library, Cuiden, IBECS, JBI, LILACS, Medline PyscoDoc, PsycoINFO, Scopus, and Web of Science databases in November 2021.”
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the information sources and the time of the last search (November 2021).
No risk-of-bias assessment methods are described in the provided abstract text.
The abstract does not report methods used to present and synthesize results.

elements.quote: “In total, 2082 publications were identified, of which 16 were included in this review.”
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies (16) but does not report total participants or summarize participant characteristics in the abstract.

elements.quote: “The mental health of out-of-hospital HPs was affected. Being a woman or having direct contact with patients showing suspicious signs of COVID-19 or confirmed cases were the factors related to a greater risk of developing high levels of stress and anxiety; in the case of depressive symptoms, it was having a clinical history of illnesses that could weaken their defenses against infection.”
elements.reason: The abstract provides results for main outcomes (stress/anxiety and depressive symptoms), but it does not provide the number of included studies/participants per outcome.
The provided evidence does not indicate that a meta-analysis was conducted or that a summary estimate with a confidence/credible interval is available from the abstract.
The abstract does not describe group comparisons with an explicit direction of effect and which group is favored.
The abstract does not briefly summarize important limitations of the included evidence.

elements.quote: “The mental health of out-of-hospital HPs was affected.”
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation/summary of findings, but it does not clearly articulate implications for practice/policy as part of a broader interpretation.
No primary funding source is stated in the provided abstract text.
No register name and registration number are provided in the provided abstract text.
No evidence in the retrieved chunks describes the current state of knowledge and important uncertainties in the rationale for the review.
No retrieved evidence explains the importance and need for conducting the review in the Introduction/Rationale.
No retrieved evidence discusses prior similar systematic reviews or explains the need for an update/replication with citations.
The retrieved evidence does not provide any rationale-level description of a proposed mechanism of action (relevant to intervention-effect reviews).
The retrieved evidence does not describe a logic model for hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes.

elements.quote: The search began with the formulation of the following research question by R.S.C., whose clinical response was possible, in PIO (Population-Intervention-Outcome) format [46]: 'Has the possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2 during the COVID-19 pandemic (I) affected the mental health (O) of HPs providing health care outside the hospital (P)?
elements.reason: The review’s objective/research question is explicitly stated and is formulated using a question-formulation framework (PIO) in the Methods section.

elements.quote: The search began with the formulation of the following research question by R.S.C., whose clinical response was possible, in PIO (Population-Intervention-Outcome) format [46]: 'Has the possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2 during the COVID-19 pandemic (I) affected the mental health (O) of HPs providing health care outside the hospital (P)?
elements.reason: The provided evidence frames the question around exposure and outcomes rather than planned intervention-effect comparisons; no planned comparisons are described as would be expected for intervention-effects reviews.

elements.quote: The selected research studies had to meet the following inclusion criteria: (1) being original, (2) based on qualitative and/or quantitative methods, (3) with any methodological design, (4) submitted for peer-review, (5) published in English, Spanish, French, Italian or Portuguese, (6) completed after December 2019, (7) without geographic limitation, (8) with at least the abstract available, and (9) that in their results evaluated the impact of possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2 on levels of stress, anxiety, depression and/or self-efficacy of the HPs who were working in public, private, or voluntary out-of-hospital EMS during the COVID-19 pandemic or identified factors related positively or negatively with these levels or compared them with those obtained in other working environments and/or professional categories.
elements.reason: Inclusion criteria are specified (study characteristics, outcomes/eligibility focus, designs/methods, and out-of-hospital EMS setting). However, the evidence does not clearly specify any follow-up requirements for eligibility.

elements.quote: The selected research studies had to meet the following inclusion criteria: ... (4) submitted for peer-review, (5) published in English, Spanish, French, Italian or Portuguese, (6) completed after December 2019, (7) without geographic limitation, (8) with at least the abstract available ...
elements.reason: Report characteristics relevant to eligibility are specified, including peer-review/report status (“submitted for peer-review”), dissemination language, and a date restriction (“completed after December 2019”).

The evidence describes reasons for exclusion (e.g., unrelated to the objective, publication format, no data from out-of-hospital HPs, low methodological quality), but it does not explicitly distinguish exclusion due to outcomes not being measured vs outcomes not being reported.

The evidence does not describe groups used in each synthesis or how such groups are linked to specific comparisons/objectives. It states that an 'Anarrative synthesis' was performed, but no synthesis grouping structure tied to comparisons is reported.

elements.quote: Opinion articles and editorials, studies of low scientific-technical quality, those that did not reply to the posed research question and/or were not in line with the objective of the review, as well as others that, despite including out-of-hospital HPs, contributed no specific data on this subgroup in their results were excluded.
elements.reason: The evidence provides rationales for notable eligibility restrictions by stating why specific types of studies (e.g., editorials/opinions, low-quality studies, not answering the question/not aligned with objective, and those lacking subgroup data) were excluded.

| Database         | Search Strategy |
elements.reason: A full search string is provided for at least some databases (e.g., CINHAL), but the evidence does not clearly show complete strategies for all databases/registers/websites/sources that were searched.

elements.quote: All the search strategies in use were developed, reproduced, and checked by three different researchers (R.S.C., R.M.C.G., and S.N.P.) for the purpose of guaranteeing the reliability of the results by comparing those obtained by each of them.

elements.quote: The search began with the formulation of the following research question by R.S.C., whose clinical response was possible, in PIO (Population-Intervention-Outcome) format [46]: 'Has the possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2 during the COVID-19 pandemic (I) affected the mental health (O) of HPs providing health care outside the hospital (P)?' From it, the Medical Subject Headings (MeSH), the Descriptors in Health Sciences (DeCS), and synonyms-free text adequate to the objective of the study were identified and combined using the Boolean operators AND and OR. In addition, some of them were truncated in order to include all possible word endings.
elements.reason: The evidence explains the initial conceptual structure in PIO and how terms were derived and combined (AND/OR, truncation), but it does not describe the final conceptual structure and explorations in full detail.

elements.quote: With regard to the selection process of the studies, from among the 99 articles considered of potential relevance, each evaluator undertook a critical reading of 25, requiring the participation of a third evaluator on 7 occasions.
elements.reason: The number of reviewers involved for critical reading of potentially relevant articles is given (each evaluator reading 25, third evaluator on 7), but the report does not provide the number of reviewers screening each record/report for all screening stages.

elements.quote: Three independent reviewers (R.S.C., R.M.C.G., and S.N.P.) screened out possible relevant studies by titles and abstracts, excluding records that did not meet the inclusion criteria.
elements.reason: Independence of reviewers is explicitly stated for title/abstract screening.

elements.quote: The final selection of the studies, the evaluation of their methodological quality, and the data-extraction was completed in pairs (N.G.S.B.-H.O.B., J.J.J.A.-J.J.F.D., A.M.R.M.-M.M.O., and M.P.M.H.-A.M.S.), independently with blind reviews, thereby resolving any possible discrepancies through consensus and, in its absence, calling for the participation of a third evaluator (R.M.C.G.).
elements.reason: Processes for resolving screening discrepancies are described (consensus; if absent, third evaluator).

elements.quote: In the face of any doubt or relevant data unavailable in the selected studies, we planned to contact the corresponding author directly, requesting the necessary clarifications.

elements.quote: Based on the research question formulated as well as the inclusion and exclusion criteria considered, the following data were specifically extracted from each selected article: title and principal author, country and year of publication, objective, type of study, place and period undertaken, size and characteristics of the sample, definition of variables under analysis and instruments used, principal results obtained, conclusions of the study and scientific-technical quality.
elements.reason: The manuscript lists the variables/data items extracted from each included study (e.g., country/year, sample characteristics, variables under analysis, instruments used, results, conclusions, and quality).

elements.quote: Critical Appraisal Tools from JBI of the University of Adelaide (Australia) [47], considered adequate for the design of the study [48,49], were used to evaluate the scientifictechnical quality of the selected articles as well as to determine the extent to which the risk of bias was reduced or eliminated in their design, performance, and/or analysis.

elements.quote: Table 3. Critical appraisal of cross-sectional studies. Y: yes; N: no; U: unclear. Q1: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined? Q2: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail? Q3: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way? elements.quote: Each individual study was classified as having a low-, moderate-, or high-risk level of bias based on the number of items answered with 'yes'. For cross-sectional studies (8 items), the methodological quality was considered low, moderate, or high if two or less, moderate if three to five, and high if six to eight criteria were met, respectively [49].
elements.reason: An overall risk-of-bias judgment (low/moderate/high) and the rules for deriving it from item responses are reported.

elements.quote: Neither a meta-analysis nor a meta-synthesis could be conducted with the studies included in the review due to the high levels of observed heterogeneity between the participants, in the area of development, in the scales and measurement instruments used, and with the final results. Furthermore, areas of uncertainty related to the scarcity of studies carried out with EMS professionals were identified since the COVID-19 pandemic is a recent event, never before experienced, which limits the scientific literature on this phenomenon. ... Anarrative synthesis of the main characteristics and findings from those studies was performed, which is summarized in Table 2.
elements.reason: The alternative synthesis approach (narrative synthesis) is described and the rationale for not performing meta-analysis/meta-synthesis (high heterogeneity and related uncertainty/scarcity) is given.

elements.quote: The findings of this review must be considered in the context of their own strengths and limitations. Its principal strength might be that no other systematic review has, to date, specifically analyzed the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the mental health of out-of-hospital HPs. As more evident limitations of this study, arising from its own methodological approach, publication bias and selection bias in the choice of the databases consulted may be mentioned, as well as the search strategy that was used and the exclusion of works published in languages other than those previously stated. An attempt was made to minimize these sorts of bias through the participation of at least 2 researchers in the search and selection process in 11 of the most relevant databases in the field of health sciences and psychology as well as the use of a somewhat unrestrictive search strategy. The methodological quality of studies selected was optimal, except in some cases, with reference to participation rates and sample representativeness, justified by the epidemiological context and the generalized difficulties imposed as a consequence of the outbreak on both HPs and the researchers themselves. The high heterogeneity observed in the socio-demographic characteristics of the sample of participants, in the field under development and in the measurement scales and instruments that were in use, complicated the comparison and any extrapolation of the results as well as the analysis of biases. Moreover, along with the relative scarcity of published studies, it must be added that a joint and not always a comparative approach was used for data analysis in most of them, without discriminating between out-of-hospital professionals and other health personnel. This living systematic review was conducted at a relatively early stage of the COVID19 pandemic.
elements.reason: The Discussion section explicitly states limitations of the review/evidence, including publication and selection bias, search strategy and language exclusions, limitations related to participation/sample representativeness, high heterogeneity, scarcity of studies, analysis approach, lack of discrimination among professional groups, and the early stage of the pandemic.
